TIER_1_INFERENTIAL.VERDICT: ZERO evidence, not weak evidence. The refreshed model beats the constant prior by 0.002047 Brier while LOSING the straight-up record 2-2 to 3-1. t = -0.0163. The 95% interval is [-0.403, +0.399] — 0.80 wide on a statistic whose entire range is [0,1]. A four-game cohort cannot separate these arms and this one does not.
TIER_1_INFERENTIAL.consequence: NO promotion. NO estimator update. The registered sample horizon is not met and the interval does not exclude zero.
TIER_1_INFERENTIAL.what_actually_happened: the refreshed model was better on CON@IND and TOR@LV and worse on POR@ATL and WSH@LAS. One game — POR@ATL, where it pushed p_home to 0.784 and Atlanta lost 101-83 — accounts for the entire deficit. The constant prior 'won' the record by having no opinion at all.
TIER_1_INFERENTIAL.why_admissible: the first and only genuinely bound cohort in the audit window. Bound on canonical id against the wehoop ARCHIVE, with the game date derived in ET via zoneinfo rather than sliced on the UTC date.
